$comment: Source manifest for the UX standards corpus. Every entry records license and reuse bucket. Bucket A may be stored and adapted; bucket A-verbatim may be stored but not modified; bucket B is link-and-restate only, never cache the prose; bucket C is excluded. Provenance SHAs captured at fetch time by fetch.mjs.

buckets.A: Openly licensed. Store verbatim, adapt freely, carry the required notice.
buckets.A-verbatim: Openly licensed for copying but NOT for derivative works. Store unmodified with the copyright notice. Do not paraphrase into a published heuristic without restating in our own words and citing.
buckets.B: Free to read, all rights reserved. Store our own restatement plus citation and URL. Never cache the source prose.
buckets.C: Excluded. Licensing or scope makes it unusable.

sources.name: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide
sources.notes: Software and Document License permits modification and derivative works. The only source supporting hard pass/fail. grid, treegrid, table, combobox, dialog, disclosure, windowsplitter and feed are the workbench-relevant patterns.

sources.name: WCAG 2.2 and Understanding WCAG 2.2
sources.notes: Normative. Approved as ISO/IEC 40500:2025. The Document License differs from the Software and Document License used by APG: copying and redistribution are permitted, derivative works are NOT. Quote it, do not rewrite it and call it ours.

sources.name: IBM Carbon Design System
sources.notes: The only enterprise design system whose documentation repo is openly licensed, so the guidance prose itself is reusable with a NOTICE. Carbon for AI covers the AI label inside a data table. data-visualization/flow-charts is the closest published guidance to lineage.

sources.name: Red Hat PatternFly
sources.notes: Closest published analogue to a data workbench. Built for enterprise consoles and used by the OpenShift console. Data view extension composes table, toolbar, pagination, filtering, sorting, selection and bulk actions into one resource-list pattern. Has a chatbot extension.

sources.name: GOV.UK Design System and Service Manual
sources.license: MIT for code; Open Government Licence v3.0 for documentation (Crown copyright)
sources.notes: OGL v3 permits copying, adapting and commercial use with an attribution statement. task-list-pages carries a researched status vocabulary (Not started / Cannot start yet / In progress / Completed) that transfers to job runs. Citizen-facing and sparse: take the writing, error handling and status discipline, not the density model.

sources.name: U.S. Web Design System
sources.license: CC0 1.0 public domain, with itemized third-party exceptions
sources.notes: Freest license, least differentiated content. Overlaps GOV.UK and is thin on density. Low priority — included because CC0 carries no attribution burden at all.

sources.name: The Eyes Have It: A Task by Data Type Taxonomy for Information Visualizations
sources.author: Ben Shneiderman
sources.notes: The Visual Information-Seeking Mantra: overview first, zoom and filter, then details on demand. More usefully, a 7 data type by 7 task taxonomy where data types include tree and network, and tasks include relate, history and extract. Those three are what most lineage UIs omit. The only citable grounding for dependency graphs.

sources.name: Cognitive Dimensions of Notations
sources.author: Thomas Green, Alan Blackwell, Marian Petre
sources.notes: The right vocabulary for query editors and notebooks, and the least-used good idea in this space. Viscosity, premature commitment, hidden dependencies, progressive evaluation, visibility, error-proneness. Out-of-order notebook execution is a hidden-dependencies failure; needing to restructure a query to add one filter is viscosity. Nielsen cannot express either.

sources.name: 10 Usability Heuristics for User Interface Design
sources.author: Jakob Nielsen
sources.license: All rights reserved, with an explicit grant to use the heuristics with attribution
sources.attribution_required: Credit Jakob Nielsen and link to https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/
sources.notes: The article states: you may use these heuristics in your own work, please credit Jakob Nielsen and provide the address for this page. That grant covers the ten principles as principles. It does NOT cover the explanatory prose, examples or posters.

sources.name: Nielsen Norman Group articles (enterprise and data-dense)
sources.license: Free to read, all rights reserved. Online reproduction is $250 per article.

key_articles.title: Data Tables: Four Major User Tasks
CASTLE Framework for Workplace Applications UX
Progress Indicators Make a Slow System Less Insufferable
10 Guidelines for Designing Your Site's AI Chatbots
The 5 Dimensions of Site-Specific AI Chatbots

sources.notes: Link and restate, never paste. Paid reports are separately licensed and forbid external redistribution — do not buy them for this corpus.

sources.name: Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction (HAX Toolkit)
sources.notes: 18 guidelines, CHI 2019 award paper, validated with 49 practitioners across 20 AI products. Organized by interaction phase: initially, during interaction, when the AI system is wrong, and over time. The wrong phase is the one most AI features ship without designing. Best-established AI UX heuristic set that exists.

sources.name: People + AI Guidebook
sources.notes: Chapters on mental models, explainability and trust, and errors and graceful failure. Current version focuses on generative AI.

sources.name: Eight Golden Rules of Interface Design
sources.author: Ben Shneiderman
sources.notes: 6th edition wording, which differs from the version usually quoted. Includes seek universal usability, prevent errors, keep users in control. Universal usability is the credible framing for the novice-versus-expert tradeoff.

sources.name: Discussing Design: Improving Communication and Collaboration through Critique
sources.author: Adam Connor and Aaron Irizarry
sources.license: Paid book. The framework is quoted in open-access secondary sources.
sources.notes: Defines the output contract for the crit tool. A well-formed critique statement identifies a specific aspect, relates it to an objective or best practice, and describes how and why. Distinguishes critique from reaction-based and directive feedback. Timing sweet spot 20 to 80 percent complete.

sources.name: An heuristic set for evaluation in information visualization
sources.author: Camilla Forsell and Jimmy Johansson
sources.license: ACM paywalled. The heuristic list is reproduced in free follow-up work.
sources.notes: The only empirically derived heuristic set built for interactive visual displays: 63 heuristics from 6 prior sets rated against 74 real infovis usability problems. Later work found it needs interaction, veracity and aesthetics added, and that evaluators lacking domain knowledge were uneasy about depth — which argues for surfacing questions rather than verdicts.

sources.name: Information Architecture Heuristics
sources.author: Abby Covert
sources.license: Free list, all rights reserved. Poster $30, workbook $20.
sources.notes: Ten principles framed by the author as a critique instrument. A data catalog is an information architecture problem, which is why this earns a place.

sources.name: Baymard Institute
sources.license: Paid, $2,400 to $8,400 per year. Terms prohibit paraphrase and automated extraction.
sources.notes: EXCLUDED. Section 3.4 forbids copying, modifying, reproducing, redistributing, republishing, paraphrasing or repackaging, and explicitly prohibits automated extraction. Section 3.3 forbids using it to derive inspiration for similar services, and they ship competing AI UX tools. Scope is homepage, category, product, cart, checkout, account. No configuration is both legal and useful.

sources.name: Atlassian Design System
sources.license: Restricted to Atlassian-interoperating products. Forbids adaptation and derivative works, documentation included.

sources.name: Shopify Polaris
sources.license: MIT plus a field-of-use rider restricting use to Shopify-interoperating applications.
sources.notes: EXCLUDED on license grounds. A maintainer confirmed non-Shopify apps may not use it even with design changes.
